item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning": The Money Issue (Aug. 2)
item.description: This week Jane Pauley hosts "The Money Issue," our annual special broadcast dedicated to the many ways in which money underscores the way we live.

item.title: Nature: Big Sur, California
item.description: We leave you this Sunday morning among nature's riches along the coast of Big Sur, Calif. Videographer: Lance Milbrand.

item.title: Hunting for sand dollars
item.description: In Florida, correspondent Martha Teichner goes searching for sand dollars – cousins of sea urchins and sea stars – with naturalist Kristen Williams (a.k.a. The Seashell Mermaid). She also goes to the California Academy of Sciences' Steinhart Aquarium in San Francisco to learn what makes these sea creatures so special. (Originally broadcast April 12, 2026.)

item.title: American Girl celebrates girl power
item.description: Founded in 1986, American Girl has created dolls, books and accessories that tell the stories of young girls in every American era. On the toy's 40th anniversary, correspondent Faith Salie explores how making history come alive is also creating timeless bonds between generations that celebrate girlhood. (Originally broadcast April 12, 2026.)

item.title: Resistance grows nationwide against AI data center boom
item.description: To fuel their artificial intelligence initiatives, tech companies are building massive numbers of AI data centers, with more than 4,000 in operation across the country. But some communities, wary of the environmental and financial implications of such facilities in their backyards, are fighting back. "Sunday Morning" national correspondent Robert Costa examines the drive to construct AI data centers, and the debate between opponents and AI advocates. (Originally broadcast April 12, 2026.)

item.title: Scarlett Johansson, skin care mogul
item.description: Actress Scarlett Johansson has played many roles in her career – and now, the Tony-winner and two-time Oscar-nominee has taken on another: launching her new line of products, called The Outset, designed for people with sensitive skin (like hers). She talks with correspondent Tracy Smith about her skin struggles, and how husband Colin Jost has been a "guinea pig" for her products. (Originally broadcast April 12, 2026.)

item.title: Does your phone eavesdrop on you?
item.description: When ads pop up on your phone for products after you've happened to mention them, is it an indication that advertisers are eavesdropping on you? Correspondent David Pogue checks out the facts about highly-targeted advertising, and why it sometimes gets weirdly specific. (Originally broadcast April 12, 2026.)

item.title: Trump calls off attack on Iran subject to peace deal being "rapidly" reached
item.description: President Trump announced Saturday night that he will cancel a pending attack on Iran after he indicated that a rough framework of a peace deal had been reached.

item.title: Fighting health care insurers
item.description: With health insurance companies frequently denying coverage for medically-requested procedures, 73 percent of Americans surveyed say healthcare delays and denials are a major problem. Now, a company called Sheer Health says they will fight insurance battles on behalf of their clients. Correspondent Susan Spencer looks at how a form of insurance against health care denials may benefit consumers. (Originally broadcast April 12, 2026.)

item.title: Bingo! New spins on an old favorite
item.description: From American Legion halls to church basements, the simplicity of Bingo and its ability to let large groups play at once is why the game raises billions of dollars for charities and non-profits. Correspondent Luke Burbank looks at the history of this popular numbers game. (Originally broadcast April 12, 2026.)

item.title: Chinese EVs pull into the lead
item.description: Last year the Chinese car company BYD (which stands for Build Your Dreams) overtook Tesla as the world's top seller of fully electric vehicles, despite the U.S. market being virtually closed to them. Correspondent Seth Doane looks at how China's long-term investments in innovation are paying off in EVs – and how protective tariffs may end up hurting American automakers down the road. (Originally broadcast April 12, 2026.)

item.title: Art made of money
item.description: Philadelphia-based artist Stacey Lee Webber has invested small coins and bills into her sculptures and jewelry – art made entirely of money. Correspondent Nancy Giles talks with the money-making artist whose creations can cost a pretty penny. (Originally broadcast April 12, 2026.)

item.title: Homebuyers chase the American Dream
item.description: A growing number of young people see themselves as "forever renters" because they can't afford to buy a home, due to short supply, higher mortgage rates, and incomes that haven't kept up with rising home prices. Correspondent Jo Ling Kent examines the difficulties of today's housing market, and checks out one Midwestern city's program aimed at attracting homebuyers from out-of-state. (Originally broadcast April 12, 2026.)

item.title: Spain's Ceuta grapples with aftermath of border surge
item.description: Dozens died, and the tiny enclave of Ceuta was thrown into chaos earlier this week after a rush of migrants entered from Morocco.

item.title: Fast-moving wildfire in Washington state prompts evacuations
item.description: The Old Trails Fire started around noon on Saturday, burning brush and grass and quickly spreading toward residential areas.

item.title: 5 killed, dozens missing after blaze breaks out on Indonesia ferry
item.description: The Mutiara Sentosa 2 ferry was traveling from Indonesia's second-largest city of Surabaya in East Java to the city of Makassar in South Sulawesi.

item.title: Flights canceled as WestJet flight attendants strike over pay dispute
item.description: WestJet canceled more than 300 flights as of early Sunday, snarling travel plans in Canada in the middle of a three-day weekend.

item.title: Moscow mayor calls deadly restaurant explosion a "terrorist act"
item.description: An explosion Saturday at a Moscow restaurant that killed three people and wounded 21 others was a bombing, Russian authorities said.

item.title: Several people killed in shooting at Idaho In-N-Out restaurant, officials say
item.description: Several people were killed in a shooting Saturday afternoon at an In-N-Out restaurant in Twin Falls, Idaho, local authorities said.

item.title: What's behind the $4B funding cut for California's high-speed rail?
item.description: Records reveal California twice missed deadlines to buy the trains at the center of a federal funding fight — then quietly dropped its lawsuit weeks after missing its new deadline.

item.title: "48 Hours" show schedule
item.description: True crime. Real justice. To miss it would be a crime.

item.title: Was Sylvie Cachay's death at Soho House an accident or murder?
item.description: An Oscar winner’s son is accused of killing his swimsuit designer girlfriend at a trendy NYC hotel.

item.title: Death at Soho House
item.description: An Oscar winner's son, a fashion designer girlfriend -- one is dead. Was it murder? "48 Hours" correspondent Troy Roberts investigates.

item.title: Rare clue at Minneapolis crime scene points to a barefoot killer
item.description: "In Minnesota here, people are not committing crimes a lot of times with the socks and shoes off," said a forensic scientist about footprints left in the victim's blood.

item.title: Bloody, bare footprints lead to decadeslong search for woman's killer
item.description: In 1993, Jeanie Childs was found stabbed more than 60 times in her Minneapolis apartment. Bloody footprints and unknown DNA left investigators without answers until a 2015 cold-case review and public DNA database finally pointed to a suspect.

item.title: Trump says deal to end Iran war may be imminent, agrees to "cancel the attack"
item.description: On Saturday, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke with Mr. Trump and cautioned him against conducting a fresh round of strikes on Iran, CBS News learned.

item.title: The Footprint
item.description: A woman is murdered in her home and the pivotal clue at the crime is a bloody footprint her killer left behind. "48 Hours" correspondent Erin Moriarty reports.

item.title: World's largest locomotive, Union Pacific's Big Boy, completes epic journey
item.description: Ian Lee traces this summer's cross-country journey of the world's largest locomotive, known as Big Boy.

item.title: 8/1: CBS Weekend News
item.description: President Trump criticizes decision to drop charges in Reflecting Pool case; Tensions rise in the Middle East.

item.title: A new high for roller coasters
item.description: Correspondent Lee Cowan reports on how the ups-and-downs of today's amusement park industry are being ridden via new technologies in roller coaster design, including the New Texas Giant (a hybrid wooden-and-steel roller coaster), and the Tormenta Rampaging Run (a "giga dive" coaster), at Six Flags Over Texas. (Originally broadcast April 12, 2026.)
